label: Google Chat
terms_note: Automation allowed inside Google Workspace organisations (the docs address Workspace only — consumer Gmail is not covered): configure a Chat app in the Cloud project; app auth uses the app's own credentials (chat.bot self-granted; chat.app.* need one-time admin approval), user auth needs the OAuth consent screen unless admin-installed / domain-wide delegated; sensitive / restricted scope classes apply. Quotas: per project 3,000 message writes/min (create / patch / delete), 60 space writes/min, 300 membership writes/min, 3,000 message reads/min, 3,000 space reads/min; per space 1 write per second (messages + space changes), 5 reaction creates/s, 15 reads/s, 10/s import; 429 → exponential back-off.

sdks: Google API client libraries + Cloud Pub/Sub for Workspace Events (developers.google.com/workspace/chat/api/reference/rest)

endpoints.call: Chat app HTTP endpoint (MESSAGE / ADDED_TO_SPACE events) or Workspace Events subscription → Pub/Sub

reference.limits: - Per project / minute: 3,000 message writes (create / patch / delete), 60 space writes (setup / create / patch / delete), 300 membership writes, 3,000 message reads, 3,000 space reads. - Per space: **1 write / second** (messages + space changes), 5 reaction creates / s, 15 reads / s, 10 / s during import. - 429 → exponential back-off. Workspace edition gates which Chat features exist (registry note: Business / Enterprise).

adapter.rate_note: Per-space write limit is 1 request per second for spaces.messages.create; reads 3,000 per minute per project (https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/limits).

fields.name: client_id
fields.help: OAuth 2.0 client id (Google Cloud console, Clients page) of the app the user consented to.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.help: The OAuth client's secret; sent with client_id, refresh_token and grant_type=refresh_token in the form body of POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token (https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server#offline).

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.help: Refresh token from a one-time authorization-code consent with access_type=offline and the scopes https://www.googleapis.com/auth/chat.messages, chat.spaces.readonly and chat.users.readstate (user authentication; app authentication needs a service-account JWT, which this runtime does not sign). 'Refresh tokens are valid until the user revokes access or the refresh token expires'; the runtime mints 1-hour access tokens from it.

me.note: Chat has no who-am-I method: spaces.list?pageSize=1 verifies the token; account carries the first space the user belongs to.

send.note: `to` is the space ID (the part after `spaces/`, e.g. AAAAAAAAAAA). With user authentication 'The content of message can only contain text'. message_id is the message resource name (spaces/…/messages/…). `subject`/`channel` are ignored.

reply.note: `channel` is the space ID (required); `thread_id` is the thread resource name spaces/{space}/threads/{thread}. REPLY_MESSAGE_FALLBACK_TO_NEW_THREAD: 'If it fails, the message starts a new thread instead'.

list_inbound.note: Lists ONE space: `channel` (space ID) is required, newest first. Chat pages by pageToken, so `page` is ignored; `since` is not sent.

get_thread.note: spaces.messages.list with filter `thread.name = spaces/{space}/threads/{thread}`: `thread_id` is that full thread name and `channel` the space ID. `page` is ignored.

mark_read.note: Sets the caller's lastReadTime in the space `channel` (space ID) to now: 'To mark the space as read, set lastReadTime to any value later (larger) than the latest message create time'. Replies inside threads are unaffected. Needs chat.users.readstate.

evidence: host chat.googleapis.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Google Trust Services)
probe: 6/6 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
spec https://chat.googleapis.com/$discovery/rest?version=v1: 6/6 tools match (path, method, parameters, body keys, response paths)
scopes chat.messages: all listed in the discovery document
